No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. Suddenly, she spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. She reaches out a hand, and Finley is sucked into her grasp.

JEN
(excitedly)
Oh, look at you! You're so beautiful!

Finley struggles and squirms in Jen's hand, but she holds tight. Jen pulls Finley out of the water and onto the beach, where Finley lies flailing on the sand.

JEN
(curiously)
What's wrong, little guy? You're not used to being out of the water, are you?

Finley looks up at Jen with a mixture of fear and confusion. Jen holds him up to the sky, and Finley's gaze follows the sun as it begins to darken.

JEN
(amused)
Oh, look! A solar eclipse! Isn't it amazing?

Finley's eyes widen in terror as the sun's corona appears, casting an otherworldly glow over the beach. Finley's body begins to convulse, and he speaks in a voice that is both familiar and yet, utterly alien.

FINLEY
(whispering)
The void... it's coming... the void is coming...

JEN
(confused)
What's wrong, Finley? You're not making any sense.

FINLEY
(urgently)
You don't understand... the horrors beyond your comprehension... the eldritch abominations that lurk beyond the veil of reality... they're coming for us all...

Finley's voice rises to a fevered pitch as he begins to speak in a language that is not of this world. Jen's eyes widen in alarm as Finley's body begins to contort and twist, his scales glistening with an eerie, greenish light.

FINLEY
(monologuing)
The Old Ones... they're stirring... the stars are aligning... the fabric of space-time is unraveling... and we're all just tiny, insignificant specks in an infinite expanse of madness...

Jen's grip on Finley tightens as he continues to speak, his words dripping with an otherworldly madness.

FINLEY
( existential crisis)
What is the meaning of existence? Is it to swim in the ocean, to feed on plankton, to breathe the air? Or is it something more? Something that transcends the mundane, the ordinary, the finite?

Finley's voice drops to a whisper, and he looks up at Jen with eyes that are no longer his own.

FINLEY
(lovecraftian horror)
I see the abyss... the void... the infinite expanse of nothingness... and I am but a tiny, insignificant speck, a mere mortal, a fleeting moment in the grand tapestry of time...

Jen's grip on Finley falters, and he slips from her grasp, falling to the sand with a soft thud. Finley's body begins to dissolve, his scales melting away like wax in a furnace.

FINLEY
(voice fading)
I am but a fish... a mere mortal... a speck of dust in the void...

The camera zooms out as Finley's body disappears into the sand, leaving Jen staring at the spot where he once was, her eyes wide with a mix of horror and awe.

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - LATER

Jen is still standing on the beach, staring at the spot where Finley disappeared. She looks up at the sky, and the solar eclipse is now complete, casting a dark, foreboding shadow over the shore.

Jen's eyes are haunted, and she knows that she will never look at the world in the same way again.

FADE TO BLACK.

THE END.
